messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: potential SRV resolution storm affecting internal service discovery in us-west-2a. Alert threshold crossed for internal DNS error rate (srv lookup failures > 8%) across multiple clusters. Escalation: oncall-priya-oc.
priya-oc: I'm on it, thanks. Can someone post the initial scope? which services showing errors?
dan-sre: seeing high SRV lookup errors from model-routing service and scheduler components. Errors manifest as ECONNREFUSED to service IPs after SRV lookup. Also intermittent increase in consul 5xx responses.
maya-net: Network telemetry shows increased retransmits on peering fabric between us-west-2a and us-west-2b starting ~2246123200. Possible ARP/flow churn.
priya-oc: ok. quick runbook steps: 1) confirm CoreDNS pods health 2) check consul leader and raft 3) throttle clients if noisy 4) consider temporary routing bypass to us-west-2b.
dan-sre: checking CoreDNS in affected clusters now.

dan-sre: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=coredns -o wide
``` 
NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE
coredns-6f8d9c7b8-2xqkz   3/3     Running   0          12d   10.2.1.45    node-a1
coredns-6f8d9c7b8-bmrvw   2/3     CrashLoop 4          3h    10.2.1.46    node-a2
```

priya-oc: one coredns pod is crashlooping on node-a2 — looks correlated with node heartbeats. Maya, is node-a2 seeing any kernel drops?
maya-net: node-a2 kernel logs show repeated netlink flaps and intermittent ifdown/ifup on eth0 at ~2246123180. Investigating fabric side.
liam-pd: Customer-facing note: models in us-west-2 may see 5-15% increased inference errors for ~20-30 minutes. We'll prepare a short status update after we stabilize.
eva-support: I'm already triaging incoming tickets, routing affected customers to degraded status. Please flag if we will open a postmortem.

priya-oc: next steps: pin traffic for critical tenants to us-west-2b where possible, scale up coredns replicas, and cordon node-a2 if it's unstable. Dan, can you add a temporary service-level TTL override for SRV lookups?
dan-sre: applying change to DNS cache TTL now.
```
# patch: reduce SRV cache TTL to 10s for affected clusters
kubectl -n kube-system apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: coredns
data:
  Corefile: |
    .:53 {
      errors
      health
      kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {
        pods insecure
        upstream
        fallthrough in-addr.arpa
      }
      cache 10
      prometheus :9153
    }
EOF
```

priya-oc: dan, once TTL change is up, scale coredns to 5 replicas in the affected AZ.
dan-sre: scaling now.
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=5
```

maya-net: fabric team toggled a slow-path to force re-sync on peering for node-a2's switch. We're seeing reduced retransmits but not fully recovered.

deploy-bot: deploy coredns scale completed 
priya-oc:  coredns scale confirmed. Cache TTL lowered. Observability — Dan, do you see SRV lookup error rate dropping?
dan-sre: error rate dropped from 12% -> 4.5% over last 2 minutes. We're still seeing intermittent consul leader 503 responses; running raft health check.

maya-net: we detected a partial hardware ASIC misbehave on switch-usw2a-12, fabric team is prepping a micro-reboot of that switch. ETA 5m. This will require short flow churn but should clear the netlink flaps.
liam-pd: agree, prefer planned micro-reboot vs node cordon if it reduces impact. Notify customers about a 5-10m maintenance bump.
eva-support: posted initial status to customers (internal ticket tracker updated).

priya-oc: plan: 1) proceed with switch micro-reboot 2) keep coredns scaled + TTL 10s 3) failover critical tenants to us-west-2b where possible via routing policy 4) monitor for 30m after switch restart then revert TTL and scale.
dan-sre: initiating canary failover for 3 critical tenants to us-west-2b now (routing policy flip).

maya-net: micro-reboot started on switch-usw2a-12. Expect 60-90s of control-plane churn.

priya-oc: heads-up: consul shows leader re-election in progress, raft committed indexes falling back. That may explain the 503s. We'll hold any writes for now.
dan-sre: confirmed consul leader stabilized to node consul-3 after 45s. 503s down to baseline. SRV error rate currently 2.1%.
liam-pd: preparing a short post for customers: root cause = transient peering fabric hardware flapping causing node heartbeats and coredns pod instability which led to increased SRV lookup failures and downstream inference errors. Mitigation = temporary TTL reduction, coredns scale, switch micro-reboot, and targeted tenant failover. No data loss. ETA for full normalcy: 30 min.
eva-support: posting update now.

priya-oc: will keep thread open for 1 hour to monitor, then close with incident summary. Add owners for postmortem: dan-sre (sre), maya-net (network), priy-oc (incident lead).

dan-sre: adding logs and metrics snapshots to incident board: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2246123456 — collecting core dumps from coredns crashloop pod for root-cause.

deploy-bot: notice: scheduled rollback of recent peering config change (PR#4521) cancelled — not necessary after reboot.

priya-oc: status at 2246127320: all checks green, SRV error rate <1%, coredns replicas stable, switch hardware flagged for follow-up with vendor. Marking incident as mitigated. Will file full postmortem in incidents channel and tag impacted tenants. Great coordination, thanks all :tada:

liam-pd: +1. I'll prepare the public-safe customer summary.

eva-support: closing customer tickets with follow-up message.

priya-oc: closing oncall handoff at 2246130800 to next oncall. Incident mitigated — moving to postmortem prep.
